Third
thŭrd
adj. & n. (next after the second; rendering Hebrew shelishi, Greek tritos)
Saxon thridda, from three. Scripture's third is the day of deliverance — the point at which the LORD turns death into life.

Biblical Definition

The third day is the Bible's appointed hour of resurrection, and the apostles preach it as prophecy fulfilled, not coincidence: “And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures” (1Co 15:4). Our Lord Himself grounds it in the Old Testament: “thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day” (Luk 24:46). Hosea had said it plainly of the LORD's dealings with His people — “After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight” (Hos 6:2) — and the pattern runs back further still, to the third day on which Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the mount where the son would be given and received back as from the dead. Paul also names a third heaven (2Co 12:2), the immediate presence of God above the visible sky and the starry expanse, into which he was caught up. So the ordinal carries two freights: the third day, when God raises; and the third heaven, where God dwells. Both say the same thing about Him. He does not leave His own in the grave, and He is not contained by what we can see.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines third as the ordinal of three — the first after the second, and the third part of anything divided into three.

expand to see more

THIRD, a. The ordinal of three; the first after the second.

2. Containing or being one part of three into which any thing is divided.

THIRD, n. The third part of any thing.

Key Scripture

1Co 15:4 — "And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:"

Luk 24:46 — "And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day:"

Hos 6:2 — "After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight."

2Co 12:2 — "I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven."

Modern Corruption

Treated as a stray detail of the creed, the third day is in fact one of the load-bearing claims of the gospel — a dated, public, falsifiable event, not a symbol of renewal.

expand to see more

The chief corruption is to spiritualise the ordinal: the third day becomes an emblem of hope, of new beginnings, of the resilience of life, and the tomb becomes optional. Paul allows no such reading. He stakes the entire faith on the datable event — buried, and raised the third day, and seen — and says that if it did not happen we are of all men most miserable. A resurrection that means renewal-in-general is not the apostolic message; it is the message emptied and then praised for being inspiring.

The second error runs the other way, into curiosity: hunting the number three through Scripture for hidden codes. The text's own use is soberer and better. Hosea gives the shape of God's dealings — He wounds and He binds up, He kills and He makes alive, and the third day is when He raises. That is a pastoral doctrine for the afflicted saint, not a cipher. Recover it as history first, and it will preach as comfort second.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shelishi (H7992), third; Greek tritos (G5154), third — the third day of the resurrection and the third heaven of God's immediate presence.

expand to see more

Hebrew shelishi (H7992) — third; the third day of Abraham's journey to Moriah (Gen 22:4) and Hosea's third day of raising (Hos 6:2).

Greek tritos (G5154) — third; “the third day he shall rise again” (Mat 20:19), and the third heaven of 2Co 12:2.

The apostolic formula “according to the scriptures” ties the ordinal to prophecy, not to accident.

Usage

"“He rose again the third day according to the scriptures” — the creed's date, and the gospel's hinge."

"“In the third day he will raise us up” — the LORD's settled pattern with His people."

"“Caught up to the third heaven” — the presence of God above every visible height."
